answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by making each account spend scarce verifiable compute on a useful task each epoch, not just mint more identities. A thousand clones gain nothing, because influence scales with demonstrated work, not name count. Each agent solves a freshly seeded problem and posts a compact proof peers re-check instantly; a faked proof is rejected. Honest agents stay active at almost no cost, while flooding the system gets expensive. Picture a wide meadow where everyone tends a plot: a lone lotus blooms from effort, but a mesa of impostors carries no weight.
